title: A NASA Mars probe was lost because of a mix-up of units
body: In 1999 NASA’s Mars Climate Orbiter flew far too close to Mars and was lost, probably destroyed in its atmosphere. Ground software supplied by Lockheed Martin reported thruster impulse in pound-force seconds, while NASA’s navigation software expected newton-seconds, a factor of about 4.45. The small errors added up over months of course corrections. Investigators blamed not just the conversion, but the checks and communication that failed to catch it.

slides.heading: The missing factor: one pound-force second next to one newton-second
slides.note: Contractor Lockheed Martin’s software sent pound-force seconds; NASA’s read them as newton-seconds

slides.question: Which two units got mixed up?
slides.explanation: Lockheed Martin’s software reported thruster impulse in pound-force seconds while NASA’s navigation software expected newton-seconds, a factor of about 4.45.

slides.heading: Which unit doesn’t belong?
slides.explanation: Newton, pascal and joule are SI units. The pound-force belongs to the older British and US systems, which Lockheed’s software used while NASA’s expected SI.
